itinerary.summary: Settle in with temples, cedar forest and café-hopping.

place.name: Hidimba Devi Temple
place.description: A four-tiered wooden pagoda temple from 1553, set in a forest of giant deodar cedars. The carvings around the doorway are the finest in the valley.

morning.tip: Queues build after 11; go straight after breakfast.

place.name: Old Manali café crawl
place.description: Cross the Manalsu bridge into the old village for slow lunches of trout and Israeli plates, apple-wood houses and Himalayan views from café terraces.

afternoon.tip: Most cafés are cash or UPI; card machines are hit and miss.

place.name: Live music night in Old Manali
place.description: Old Manali's cafés host acoustic sets and open-mic nights through the season, the easiest way to meet other travellers.

evening.tip: Places close by 11 PM under local rules; plan your walk back down.

itinerary.summary: Atal Tunnel to Sissu, then snow play at Solang Valley.

place.name: Atal Tunnel and Sissu
place.description: Drive through the 9-km Atal Tunnel under the Rohtang Pass into Lahaul's stark valley, with frozen waterfalls and snow fields around Sissu.

morning.tip: Hire a local taxi; private Manali taxis are the only ones with valley permits. Check road status the night before.

place.name: Solang Valley
place.description: Snow slopes for sledging, skiing lessons and paragliding in season, with the ropeway climbing to 3,200 m.

afternoon.tip: Rent snow boots and jackets at Solang, not in Manali; it's cheaper and you avoid carrying them.

place.name: Dinner on the Mall Road
place.description: Back in town, walk the pedestrian Mall and eat Himachali siddu and trout at one of the dhabas off the main strip.

evening.tip: Siddu, a steamed stuffed bread with ghee, is the local dish to order.

itinerary.summary: Rafting on the Beas and hot springs at Vashisht.

place.name: White-water rafting on the Beas
place.description: A 14-km run of grade II-III rapids from Pirdi, the classic Kullu rafting stretch, with guides and gear included.

morning.tip: Rafting runs roughly Mar-Jun and Sep-Oct; it stops during the monsoon.

place.name: Kullu shawl weavers
place.description: Stop at the Bhuttico weavers' co-operative to see handlooms and buy a genuine Kullu shawl with its geometric border.

afternoon.tip: Co-op prices are fixed and the wool is genuine, unlike many roadside shops.

place.name: Vashisht hot springs
place.description: Soak in the sulphur hot-spring baths beside the old Vashisht temple, then dinner in the village.

evening.tip: The public baths are separate for men and women; bring a towel.

itinerary.summary: A half-day hike to Jogini Falls before heading home.

place.name: Jogini Falls hike
place.description: A 3-km trail from Vashisht through apple orchards and pine forest to a 150-m waterfall sacred to the local goddess.

morning.tip: Wear proper shoes; the last stretch is rocky and slippery.

place.name: Manu Temple and Old Manali lunch
place.description: The temple to the sage Manu, who gave Manali its name, sits at the top of the old village. One more café lunch before the road.

afternoon.tip: Book overnight Volvo buses to Delhi a few days ahead in peak season.

place.name: Van Vihar riverside walk
place.description: A deodar park along the Beas for a last easy walk and paddle-boating on the small lake before your evening bus.

evening.tip: Overnight buses leave from the private bus stand near the Mall around 5-7 PM.

stays.name: Zostel Manali
stays.why: The social hub for friend groups, with dorms and private rooms and a big common area.

stays.name: Johnson Lodge
stays.why: Comfortable rooms and a well-loved restaurant, walkable to the Mall.

stays.name: Old Manali homestays
stays.why: Wooden village houses with orchard views, good value for a group.

essentials.currency: Indian Rupee (INR). UPI and cards work in towns; carry cash for small temples, coracles and rural stalls.
essentials.language: Hindi and Kullui; English widely understood
essentials.tipping: Round up; tip rafting guides ₹100-200 each
essentials.weather: Apr is crisp (5-20°C) with snow above Solang. Dec-Feb is freezing; Jul-Aug brings landslide risk.
essentials.gettingAround: Overnight Volvo from Delhi (12-14 h) or fly to Bhuntar (50 km). Local taxis for Solang and Atal Tunnel.
essentials.phrase: Ram Ram: the everyday Himachali hello

packing: Warm layers and a down jacket

summary.overview: Four days in the Kullu valley with your crew: Old Manali cafés, a day in the snow at Solang and Atal Tunnel, river rafting in Kullu and a hike to Jogini Falls.
highlights: Snow at Solang Valley and through Atal Tunnel
Old Manali's cafés and live music
The Jogini Falls hike from Vashisht
